source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.
historical_synonyms_documented: Quercus virginiana Mill. var. fusiformis (Small) Sarg.

morphology_documented.habit: Evergreen shrub to large tree, can spread through root sprouts
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate simple evergreen leathery leaves (genus); blades generally broad near base and rounded basally, rather than cuneate like Q. virginiana
morphology_documented.flowers: Spring, monoecious; drooping staminate catkins and pistillate short spikes (genus)
morphology_documented.fruit: Fusiform acorns (17–)20–30(–33) mm long, generally longer than wide, acute tip, usually extend more than half their length beyond the cup
morphology_documented.habitat: Limestone outcrops and well-drained, generally xeric habitats

source_scope_note: Species vs genus/key-level characters distinguished in text; no undocumented characters inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historic synonym Q. virginiana var. fusiformis; flora recognizes separate species but discusses extensive hybridization and introgression
Q. virginiana comparison has usually ovoid, round-ended acorns 15–20(–25) mm long, versus longer fusiform acorns here
preservation: Additive research record, existing species cards, original media, credits and galleries unchanged
